title: Sleeping, unresponsive, yet possibly still hearing

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
The record must not be used to diagnose, time, or manage a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, and emergency decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: A dying person sleeps for long stretches or no longer answers, while people in the room wonder whether speaking, music, touch, or quiet presence can still reach them.
ordinary_language_queries: can they hear me if unconscious
should I keep talking to dying parent
he stopped talking can he hear us

content_layers.observation_text: Public sources repeatedly advise families that a person who is drowsy, asleep, or no longer speaking may still be able to hear or feel them, while avoiding certainty about any individual case.
content_layers.source_synthesis: NCI, NHS inform, Palliative Care Australia, Marie Curie, and healthdirect converge on a cautious public message: do not assume non-response means absence of hearing; speak softly, normally, or use touch if wanted and appropriate.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This is a core DeathVocab threshold moment: the room changes from conversation to address. The future corpus should collect the exact words people use when they speak to someone who may not answer.

what_this_is_not: not proof that the person consciously understands every word
not an instruction to force talk, touch, prayer, or music
not a claim that hearing is always preserved
not a substitute for consent-sensitive cultural or family boundaries
uncertainties: What the dying person actually experiences cannot usually be known from public sources.
Some people may not want touch, music, prayer, or constant speech; prior wishes and cultural frame matter.
The lay surface must avoid converting possibility into certainty.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should say: it is reasonable to keep speaking gently or offering quiet presence, but no one has to perform at the bedside and silence can also be care.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect bedside scripts for inviting families to speak without pressuring them and for protecting the dying person from overstimulation.
language_notes: Use “may still hear” rather than “can hear everything.”
Treat “say goodbye” as an invitation, not an obligation.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the v2 witnessed-moment schema. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical safety review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent or worried readers to qualified local support.
